english.notes:
(i) This offence should not be used after 11:55pm on 18th July 2021, as per SI 2021/848.
(ii) Please note - whilst this is a summary offence, the offence is not governed by the 6 month time limit that would usually apply to offences as set out in section 127(1) of the Magistrates Court Act 1980. This is because the offence is created by regulations made under the Public Health (Control of Disease) Act 1984. Section 64A of the Public Health (Control of Disease) Act 1984 provides the time limits for this offence, being before the end of the period of 6 months beginning with the date on which evidence which the prosecutor thinks is sufficient to justify the proceedings comes to the prosecutor's knowledge; and within 3 years of the date of the commission of the offence.
(ii) Regulation 3(3) further provides that: If an offence under this regulation committed by a body corporate is proved -
(a) to have been committed with the consent or connivance of an officer of the body, or
(b) to be attributable to any neglect on the part of such an officer,
the officer (as well as the body corporate) is guilty of the offence and liable to be prosecuted and proceeded against and punished accordingly.
(iii) Regulation 4 deals with the issue of FPN where the amount specified is £1000. However, regulation 4(7) stipulates that the FPN must specify that if £500 is paid before the end of the period of 14 days following the date of the notice that is the amount of the fixed penalty. Furthermore, regulation 4(8) also provides that a second fixed penalty notice issued is £2000; in the case of the third £4,000 and in the case of a fourth and subsequent fixed penalty notices received, £10,000. An authorised person may issue the FPN which includes a constable or PCSO, so police/PCSO can issue FPN for this offence.
